Center for Ocean Innovation Project Statistics: • The University proposes to build a Center for Ocean Innovation on URI land at either the Allen Harbor site or Narragansett Bay Campus. COURSE REPORT Special Summer Curriculum Committee Report 2026-2027-SSCC-01-A At the July 14, 2026 meeting of the Special Summer Curriculum Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate Executive Committee for approval. informational matters TEMPORARY COURSE BPS346X: Self-Paced Skills Laboratory for Pharmaceutical Scientists, Fall 2026 (2 crs.) Explores core experimental techniques used in biomedical and pharmaceutical research.
Supports students before or during independent research, and emphasizes practical skill development, quantitative reasoning, and the connection between experimental data and biological or pharmacological questions.
Students will learn how to design assays, generate and analyze data, and evaluate experimental results with an emphasis on accuracy, reproducibility, and good laboratory practice.
Students will select specialized experimental modules aligned with their research interests or future laboratory placements.

By the end of the course, students will work more independently and effectively in biomedical or pharmaceutical research laboratories, with a strong foundation in experimental technique, data analysis, and scientific communication. (Lab. 3) Pre: BPS345 and permission by the chair of BPS. for confirmation by the senate NEW COURSES BPS493: Scholars in Biomedical & Pharmaceutical Sciences, Fall 2026 (1 cr.) Student forum to present research projects, discuss experimental design and results, and engage in scientific dialogue with peers and faculty.
Research topics may span areas such as drug discovery, pharmacology, toxicology, pharmaceutics, pharmacokinetics, environmental health, and natural products.
Through structured presentations and discussion, students develop skills in scientific communication, data interpretation, and critical evaluation of research.
Exposes participants to diverse research approaches within pharmaceutical sciences, helping students connect laboratory research with concepts

learned in the classroom.
Students will strengthen their ability to present scientific work professionally, ask thoughtful questions, and engage in scholarly discussion—skills essential for graduate study, professional programs, and careers in biomedical research. (Seminar) Pre: BPS194, BPS250, credit or concurrent enrollment in BPS345.
May be repeated for a maximum of 4 credits.
S/U only for students not concurrently enrolled in an independent study.

President DATE: April 4, 2024 SUBJECT: Initial Review of the FY 2026 - FY 2030 Capital Improvement Plan Purpose of Submittal: Each year, as the General Assembly is considering the enactment of the budget for the upcoming fiscal year (FY25), we also begin the budget request cycle for the following year (FY26).
The first budget submittal i n the cycle, in July each year, is the Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) which is a rolling five -year plan of proposed University capital projects of $1 million or more funded with unrestricted funds together with related requests for State funding.
The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees has two opportunities to review the proposed CIP, first at the April Board meeting as an item for review and discussion, and next at the June Board meeting for final approval and submission to the State Office o f Management and Budget (OMB).

This submittal is a discussion with the Board in preparation for review and approval at the June Board of Trustees meeting.
Points to Consider: The enclosed presentation provides updates to existing CIP projects scope/budget/schedule, including the Narragansett Bay Campus Phase 1 and 2 projects, the Fine Arts Center, the Athletics Complex Renewal, the Biomedical Sciences Building, and New Undergra duate Housing.
It also provides updated cost information for the Memorial Union and Health and Counseling Center projects which have been on hold for the last several years to prioritize housing.
The presentation also highlights several proposed additions to the CIP, with a heavy emphasis on addressing the significant backlog of asset renewal needed on URI’s buildings, which in total comprise 28% of the State’s buildings.
These additions include improving campus accessibility, access control, and building envelope integrity, and refurbishment of the Carothers Library HVAC systems and the university’s water tower.
Additional new projects include the replacement of graduate housing and moving URI’s automotive shop to accommodate undergraduate housing expansion.

Finally, the CIP includes a new project to address destabilization of the access road to the newly completed NBC pier due to significant recent storm damage.
The presentation also notes that given URI’s plans to undertake a Campus Master Plan this year, we do not intend to identify a 2026 GO Bond project in this year’s CIP.
We do intend to submit a GO Bond project in next year’s CIP, when it will be required for consideration by the General Assembly.
Supporting Information: See Enclosure.
CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PLAN FY26-FY30 Presentation to URI Board of Trustees Finance & Facilities Committee April 4, 2024

What is the Capital Improvement Plan? •5 Year plan that shows projects that have a total project cost of greater than $1 Million •It is a rolling plan that is submitted annually as a request to the state, typically on July 1st. Who Approves the Capital Improvement Plan? •There are 5 levels of approval. They are: • University of Rhode Island -Facilities Committee (internal) (April & May) • University of Rhode Island -President’s Executive Council (March & June) • University of Rhode Island -Board of Trustees (April & June) • Executive Branch • Analysis performed and Recommendations made by the Office of Management and Budget (July-December) • Final Approval by Governor’s Office (Third week of January) • Legislative Branch • Analysis performed and Recommendations made by both the House and Senate Fiscal Offices (January –June) • Final Plan approved as part of the RI Budget Appropriations Bill (June) How is a project added to the Capital Improvement Plan? •In order toreceive consideration, all projects must be submitted on the Capital Improvement Request form by a member of the Senior Leadership to the URI Office of Planning & Real Estate Development •Most projects will have an advanced planning study performed prior to inclusion in the Capital Improvement plan to determine program, siting, massing, and total expected project cost
What does the Capital Improvement Plan cover? The University of Rhode Island’s Board of Trustees is responsible for about 28% of the State’s total real estate portfolio.

New CIP Projects THE UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND

New Projects: (in recommended priority order) • Campus Accessibility–This project, would provide dedicated resources to improve campus access to persons with disabilities.
Projects include restroom improvements, exterior pedestrian improvements, and discrete building improvements such as elevator modernizations.
URI has 80 elevators.
Of these, 19 are more than 30 years old and only 18 are newer than 10 years.
Many of our buildings are served by single units.
The combination of single units and aged equipment often results i n downtime and limits access.
This level of support would allow for the modernization of 2 -3 units per year or the replacement of one.
Funding source is RICAP -$16.5MM (FY26/27 @ $3MM FY28-30 @ $3.5MM each year) • Building Envelope Improvements–Many of the campus buildings have envelopes, including roofing systems, that are far past their serviceable life.
With water intrusion active in many locations, protecting these facilities from the damage that this causes and ensuring that environmental conditions remain safe for occupancy, this project addresses critical concerns now present on campus.

Funding source is RICAP -$53MM over 4 years • Carothers HVAC Replacement–The initial core structure of the Library was constructed in 1965 and renovated in two supplemental phases in the early ‘90s.
The current structure is 252,792 gross square feet on five floors with 175 assignable spaces.
Many air handling units are original to the building, have well exceeded their expected 30 -year lifetime, and are in relatively poor condition which can adversely affect air quality.
Funding source is RICAP -$64.3MM starting in FY26 • Campus Access Control–Current evaluation of a university-wide Access Control systems is underway.
In order to provide a safer campus environment, there will be a need to update the software and hardware systems to allow for a secure campus and quick responses to emergencies such as lockdown for an active shooter event.
Total Project Cost and Schedule TBD.
Funding source is RICAP -$1.5MM (just FY26) for initial conversion to a uniform system for the campus.
Future support will be needed to tie in all buildings to this centralized system over time.
Future support level TBD

Campus Accessibility Project Statistics: • This project, would provide dedicated resources to improve campus access to persons with disabilities. Projects include restroom improvements, exterior pedestrian improvements, and discrete building improvements such as elevator modernizations. URI has 80 elevators. Of these, 19 are more than 30 years old and only 18 are newer than 10 years. Many of our buildings are served by single units. The combination of single units and aged equipment often results in downtime and limits access. This level of support would allow for the modernization of 2-3 units per year or the replacement of one. • $ 16,500,000 –RICAP • Status: Pending Funding Approval • Start 2025 • Complete 2030 Elevator Modernization FY26 Request Accessibility Improvements
